beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process reads and updates windowed features repeatedly.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image representation from the compact recurrent computation. The encoder first turns the low-resolution input into features. Those features are partitioned into windows before the thought process runs. DQ-CTM then reads and updates the carrier through shared ticks. The same DQ-CTM parameters are reused at each tick. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through shared thought ticks
params.note: Dense carrier persists while compact thought updates it.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first creates a dense feature field, then partitions that field into windows without discarding tokens.
beats.narration: The equation defines the dense carrier before the recurrent thought process sees it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window partition operates on that field and keeps the tokens available for processing.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded before it is windowed

window partition that keeps every token

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; its 1.129 million parameters are second largest among the five methods.
beats.claim: Table 1 reports Params for CATANet 0.535M, RFDN 0.550M, IMDN 0.715M, DQ-CTM-SR 1.129M, and CARN 1.592M.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison puts ThinkSR between the smallest transformer baseline and the largest CNN baseline. CATANet is the smallest entry at just over half a million parameters. RFDN is nearly the same size at zero point five five million. IMDN is larger, but still below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR reaches one point one two nine million, the second largest of the five. CARN is the largest model in this table at one point five nine two million.
